title: A Small Room of Color
summary: A compact entry about a concentrated exhibition space where color does most of the narrative work.
main_text:
The smallest room in the building turned out to have the strongest pulse. It was crowded with color but not chaotic, as if each piece had been chosen to test a slightly different emotional register. Warm ochres held one wall together, while greens and pinks unsettled the next in useful ways.

Because the room was so small, every painting entered into conversation with its neighbors. A bold red looked louder after a muted landscape. A pale interior scene gained fragility beside a thickly painted abstract panel. The scale forced comparison and made color feel active rather than decorative.

I stayed longer than expected because the room kept recomposing itself every time I turned. It proved that size has little to do with intensity. Sometimes a small room is exactly what color needs to become impossible to ignore.
